skill.name: set-up-cloudflare-chatgpt-ads-customer-matching
skill.description: Guide customer matching for ChatGPT Ads on a Cloudflare website using Product Metrics. Check tracking, configure the consent banner, and verify conversion delivery with a test order.
skill.summary: Set up and verify consent-based customer matching for ChatGPT Ads on Cloudflare.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts reflect documentation, read-only setup checks, or routine use of Product Metrics. Confirmed risks involve write approval, broad order lookups, and an installer without a fixed version. The workflow also leaves gaps in credential handling, browser handoffs, Cloudflare permission review, and disclosure of customer data sharing.

remediation.issue: The command-line workflow conflicts with instructions to keep API keys out of chat.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct entry in the trusted dashboard or a documented secret-input mechanism. Do not put credentials in chat or command arguments.

remediation.issue: Write instructions do not require confirmation of the target or effects.
remediation.suggestion: Before changes or retries, confirm the property, destination, and effect with the operator. Retry only the same approved request with its original key.

remediation.issue: Order lookups can expose records unrelated to the test.
remediation.suggestion: Use delivery status first. When order details are necessary, request a known test order ID and return only fields needed for the check.

remediation.issue: The install command does not pin the installer or the skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Document a verified installer version and immutable skill revision. Require separate approval before running any installation.

remediation.issue: Browser handoff URLs are relayed without a destination check.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and verify the expected provider domain before sharing a handoff URL. Direct the user to the known dashboard if validation fails.

remediation.issue: Cloudflare troubleshooting asks the operator to approve every permission.
remediation.suggestion: List the required scopes and their purpose. Have the operator confirm the intended account and zone and stop if unexpected permissions appear.

remediation.issue: Matching can start with destination activation, but the delivery test covers only accepted consent.
remediation.suggestion: Before enabling sending, disclose which fields are shared and review the consent mapping. Test both accepted and declined consent with controlled orders.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting API Key Handling Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows taking an OpenAI API key from the operator and passing it to a command. The reference explicitly forbids pasting it into chat.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: No secure command input is specified. An agent may ask for the key in chat or expose it through process arguments or tool logs.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Browser Handoff
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the operator to open a URL returned by a tool without requiring a scheme or domain check. A compromised response could redirect the operator to an unrelated sign-in page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The browser handoff is explicit, and the instruction does not constrain the returned destination. No evidence of a malicious URL was found.

semantic_findings.title: Blanket Cloudflare Permission Approval
semantic_findings.description: The guide tells operators to approve every permission when authorization fails. The integration adds tracking across the domain, but the guide does not list required scopes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction discourages checking individual permissions. The guide does not establish that any actual scope is excessive.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Matching Without a Consent Denial Test
semantic_findings.description: Connecting the destination can enable matching without a separate switch. The test accepts all cookies and cannot verify suppression for visitors who decline or show which identifiers were sent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide documents unhashed IP addresses and unmodified browser references alongside hashed email. It verifies delivery only with consent granted, not the denied path.

content.user_title: Set Up ChatGPT Ads Customer Matching on Cloudflare
content.value_statement: Cookie-based tracking can miss conversions from your Cloudflare storefront. Use Product Metrics to check consent settings and verify delivery of conversion events that can include customer matching data.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP server and identify the next setup step.
Guide the operator through Cloudflare authorization and ChatGPT Ads destination setup when tracking is missing.
Check which consent banner Product Metrics is configured to use.
Explain when matching events can include hashed email, IP address, user agent, and click or browser references.
Guide a test order and interpret the destination status, delivery counts, and reported errors.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, editor or admin access, a proxied Cloudflare storefront, and access to ChatGPT Ads Manager.
The operator must complete Cloudflare authorization and any campaign optimization changes in the browser.
Delivery checks do not reveal the hashed fields or prove that an event matched a person.
Historical orders are not imported, and later refunds or cancellations do not revise events already sent.

use_cases.title: Check Storefront Readiness
use_cases.description: Find out whether your storefront already has the tracking and destination needed for customer matching.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Conversions
use_cases.description: Use a known test order and destination status to check delivery without pulling unrelated order records.

use_cases.title: Review Consent And Data Sharing
use_cases.description: Check the selected banner and identify which customer fields may be shared before approving live sending.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: You are planning setup for one Cloudflare storefront.
prompt_templates.prompt: List the prerequisites for ChatGPT Ads customer matching on my Cloudflare storefront. Tell me what to check in each dashboard without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find The Next Step
prompt_templates.scenario: Your Product Metrics property may already have tracking enabled.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read setup status for my selected Product Metrics property. Tell me what is complete and which dashboard step comes next. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Review Consent Before Sending
prompt_templates.scenario: You need to approve a banner configuration before activating the destination.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check which banner is configured for my storefront. Explain which event fields depend on each consent choice. Wait for approval before changing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Controlled Delivery Test
prompt_templates.scenario: You need to check delivery and the expected behavior when consent is declined.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan tests for accepted and declined marketing consent. Use only the test order IDs I provide. Explain what delivery results can and cannot verify.

output_examples.input: What is still missing before we can check customer matching?
output_examples.output: The Cloudflare gateway is active, but the ChatGPT Ads destination is not connected. Review consent first, then enter your Pixel ID and key in the Product Metrics dashboard.

output_examples.input: The test order arrived. Does that prove customer matching worked?
output_examples.output: The destination received the test order. This confirms delivery, but the dashboard does not show which hashed fields were sent or whether a person matched.

best_practices: Verify the storefront, Cloudflare zone, Product Metrics property, and Pixel ID before authorizing changes.
Enter the Conversions API key directly in the trusted dashboard. Keep it out of chat and command arguments.
Check the banner and run controlled tests for both granted and declined marketing consent.
anti_patterns: Approving all requested Cloudflare permissions without reviewing the account, zone, and scopes.
Listing live customer orders when destination status or a known test order is enough.
Treating hashed identifiers as anonymous or successful delivery as proof of matching.

faq.question: Do I need a separate switch for customer matching?
faq.answer: No. The guide describes matching data as part of eligible events once the ChatGPT Ads destination is connected.

faq.question: Which consent banners does the guide support?
faq.answer: Product Metrics lists OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano for Cloudflare Tracking.

faq.question: What customer information can a Cloudflare event include?
faq.answer: It can include a hashed email when your site supplies it, plus IP address, user agent, and click or browser references.

faq.question: What happens when a visitor declines consent?
faq.answer: Without marketing consent, no event is sent. Click and browser references also require ad storage consent. Without ad personalization consent, an eligible event is marked as opted out.

faq.question: Where should I enter the Conversions API key?
faq.answer: Enter it directly in the Product Metrics OpenAI connection form. Do not send it in chat.

faq.question: Can I confirm which customer identifiers matched?
faq.answer: No. The guide checks event delivery and errors. It does not provide a report of hashed fields or individual matches.
